title: Like a 'vertical roller coaster': Simulating flight FZ1073's sudden plunge
gist: Reuters (via Al-Monitor) recreated in a simulator the 16,000-foot, roughly 30-second plunge of flydubai flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Israel after its Omani co-pilot, reportedly Hammam al-Hammami, attacked the captain with a crash axe in what the UAE prosecutor general called a 'terrorist attack'; the Boeing 737 MAX 8 withstood the strain, drawing praise from Trump, while details emerged of the co-pilot's training history and Australian links.

insights.claim: Flydubai flight FZ1073, bound for Israel from Dubai, plunged 16,000 feet in about 30 seconds after the co-pilot attacked the captain with an emergency crash axe, an incident the UAE prosecutor general called a 'terrorist attack'.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: An insider attack on a UAE-Israel route raises aviation security and insurance concerns for Gulf carriers serving Israel.
insights.quote: plunged 16,000 feet in about 30 seconds before being levelled out and landing safely

insights.claim: The plane was levelled out after passengers overpowered the co-pilot, and a reserve crew of pilots onboard landed it; the captain was the only one hurt.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: The presence of reserve pilots was decisive, likely fueling debate on cockpit crew requirements and insider-threat protocols.
insights.quote: This was nothing but a miracle that nothing was hurt apart from the captain

insights.claim: Simulator recreation by aviation instructor Alberto Paduanelli indicates the autopilot disconnected before the plunge began, causing rapid acceleration; he compared the experience to a 'very, very vertical roller coaster' with negative g-forces lifting unstrapped passengers from seats.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Technical detail relevant to the investigation of the flight path and passenger injury risk.
insights.quote: the aircraft's autopilot disconnected before the plunge began, causing the jet to accelerate rapidly
insights.locator: Using a simulator to recreate the incident

insights.claim: US President Donald Trump praised the Boeing 737 MAX for withstanding G forces and strain 'far beyond what it was designed and expected to do' during the FZ1073 incident; Boeing did not comment.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: A rare positive narrative for the 737 MAX's structural integrity, though unverified by Boeing or investigators.
insights.quote: was able to withstand G Forces and Strain far beyond what it was designed and expected to do

insights.claim: Paduanelli said a prolonged high-speed dive can place extreme strain on an airframe, even though aircraft are designed and tested to withstand substantial aerodynamic loads.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: The airframe will likely require detailed structural inspection; extent of damage remains unknown.

insights.claim: Two sources told Reuters the co-pilot was Hammam al-Hammami, an Omani national; UAE authorities did not confirm and Oman had yet to comment.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: An Omani perpetrator could create diplomatic friction between Gulf states and complicate Gulf-Israel aviation links.
insights.quote: The co-pilot was identified as ‌Hammam al-Hammami, an Omani national

insights.claim: Royal Air Maroc said al-Hammami did three months of training with it in 2025 but his job application was rejected; Buckinghamshire New University said he took a distance-learning aviation management course but no pilot training; Australian Federal Police are investigating his 'links to Australia', with a source saying he studied at a Melbourne university.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Questions about pilot vetting and hiring standards at flydubai may follow, with reputational and regulatory implications.
insights.quote: his application to work there afterwards was rejected
